text:
maria: FYI our CI S3 usage spiked again — the nightly perf job uploaded 120GB of nsys traces. Can we tighten the harvest policy? :grimacing:
kevin: yep saw that. most of those traces are full-sequence runs with identical kernels. we should dedupe + sample by kernel-hotspot to cut size by ~5x.
ryan: honest question — do we need raw .qdrep for every run? we could store nsys export of kernel timeline + a compressed perfetto instead. raw qdrep is huge.
anjali: +1 on smarter sampling. proposal: keep full nsys for canary runs only (every 3 days), otherwise store summarized timeline + top-10 kernels flamegraph. small text artifacts for quick diffs.
kevin: sounds good. also think about prefix-based caching for KV traces — if the KV cache is warm, runs are mostly idle. we should capture KV hit histogram instead of whole GPU timeline for those cases.
maria: @trace-bot can we update the nightly job to do: 1) run nsys with --sample CPU+CUDA 2) post-process to extract kernel timeline JSON 3) gzip timeline and upload 4) drop raw qdrep unless tag==canary?
trace-bot: ack — I can implement steps 1–3. need the postproc script + where to flag canary. give me the path or a script snippet.
ryan: here's a tiny postproc snippet that worked locally:
```bash
nsys profile -o run.qdrep --trace=nvtx,cuda ...
nsys export --format=json --output=timeline.json run.qdrep
python tools/trace_summarize.py timeline.json --top 10 --kv-hist > summary.json
gzip -c timeline.json > timeline.json.gz
# upload summary.json + timeline.json.gz
```
kevin: trace_summarize.py should include kernel fingerprinting (name + duration median + occ count) so diffs are stable. We had a flaky diff because p50 moved by a few microseconds and the diff flagged a regression.
anjali: we should normalize durations by sequence length too — long sequences will naturally bump durations. add seq_len to the fingerprint and store per-100-token normalized times.
maria: great notes. retention policy draft: keep summary.json forever, timeline.json.gz for 14 days, qdrep for canary tags for 30 days. auto-prune older than policy. also add an env var CI_PERF_STORE=redwood-perf-prod.
kevin: + add a small manifest with metadata: {run_id, model, seq_len_dist, kv_warm_pct, commit, job_tag}. that'll help dashboard diffs.
anjali: about gating — we shouldn't block PRs on nightly artifacts, but we can post automatic regression alerts to the perf-diffs dashboard and ping the responsible engineer if p95 latency regresses >5%.
ryan: one more ops ask: the postproc should compute kernel selection sanity checks e.g., verify the chosen kernels match the compiled kernel map for the model variant, attach a flag if fallback kernels were used. that helps catch rollout regressions.
trace-bot: implemented the upload flow to s3://redwood-perf-ci/nightlies/{date}/{run_id}/ with manifest.json, summary.json, timeline.json.gz. skipping qdrep unless CANARY=true. will open a PR with the job changes.
sre-bot: cost note: with the proposed retention we estimate S3 delta of -78% (rough calc). also enabling server-side compression on uploads reduces size another ~40% on timeline json.
maria: thanks all. @kevin @anjali @ryan please review the PR when it's up. I'll schedule a canary run for tomorrow morning to validate end-to-end. :thumbsup:
